record.paper_title: Open questions in massive star research
record.original_question: What physical mechanism powers superluminous supernovae, especially the common hydrogen-poor Type Ic events and the still poorly understood hydrogen-rich subclass? The unresolved task is to distinguish among power from several solar masses of radioactive nickel produced in pair-instability explosions, conversion of ejecta kinetic energy into light through collision with dense circumstellar matter, and energy injection from a newly born millisecond magnetar, while also determining whether chemically homogeneous low-metallicity massive stars are truly the progenitors of the magnetar-powered Type Ic events.

evidence.quote: Three different types of explanations for their high luminosity have been put forward.

However, so far chemically homogeneously evolving stars have not yet been unambiguously identified, which leaves a big open question for this scenario. Furthermore, there are other types of SLSNe, most remarkably the hydrogen-rich SLSNe, for which the origin is not yet clarified (e.g., Kangas et al. 2022).

artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (2023–2025) continues to debate the dominant power source of SLSNe. New observations such as Lense–Thirring-precessing magnetar models, light curves explained by pulsational pair-instability circumstellar shells, and studies of hydrogen-rich events like SN 2023gpw all indicate the question is still unresolved, with no unambiguous identification of chemically homogeneously evolving progenitors.

status_evidence.title: Lense–Thirring precessing magnetar engine drives a superluminous supernova
status_evidence.snippet: Most SLSNe-I light curves have several bumps that are unexplained by the standard magnetar model.
status_evidence.claim: Standard magnetar model remains incomplete for SLSNe-I; mechanism still debated.

status_evidence.title: SN 2023gpw: exploring the diversity and power sources of hydrogen-rich superluminous supernovae
status_evidence.snippet: Diversity and power sources of hydrogen-rich SLSNe.
status_evidence.claim: Hydrogen-rich SLSN power source still under investigation in 2025.

status_evidence.title: A superluminous supernova lightened by collisions with pulsational pair-instability shells
status_evidence.snippet: Modeled by successive interactions with multiple circumstellar shells of total mass ~6.8–7.7 solar masses.
status_evidence.claim: CSM interaction with pulsational pair-instability shells remains a competing model.
